note: The ROUTE half of the authz-contract gate (scripts/check-authz-guards.mjs, ADR-246/ADR-275).
Every Route Handler (a `route.ts|tsx` file under app/ — Next 16 file convention, see
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/15-route-handlers.md) must carry an
EXPLICIT authorization verdict. A handler earns one of two ways:
1. MACHINE-DETECTED — EVERY exported HTTP method reaches a recognised gate (ROUTE_GATE in
check-authz-guards.mjs: requireAdmin / assertOwner / getCallerProfile / auth.getUser /
rejectUnauthorizedCron / verify…Signature / webhooks.constructEvent / …), the gate is not
inside an if/else/switch/catch branch, and nothing queries through the RLS-bypassing admin
client above it (R1/R2/R3, ADR-1070). Nothing is recorded here for those.
2. HUMAN-ASSERTED — an entry below. These routes have NO route-level gate, by design. The
verdict is a person's reading of the code on the `checked` date. It is NOT proof.
This file is therefore a DEBT LEDGER, not a certificate. Read every entry that way.
A GATE TOKEN THAT DOES NOT GATE BELONGS HERE, NOT IN THE CODE (ADR-1070). Three routes were moved
into this file on 2026-08-17 for exactly that reason: each called a real gate on one branch, or
after a service-role read, and was therefore green for a line that authorized nothing. Deleting
that line would have flipped them red without changing one byte of their authorization. An entry
here is the stronger record — a reason a person wrote, pinned to the body by a digest.
WHY THE DIGEST. `digest` pins the route's normalised body (comments and blank lines stripped,
sha256, first 16 hex). The whole complaint that opened LIVE-022 was that the 2026-08-04 hand
audit was clean on the day and 'nothing catches a bad one tomorrow'. The digest is tomorrow:
edit a ledgered route's CODE and the gate fails until a human re-reads it and re-records the
verdict. Prose edits above the code do not trip it, because the verdict is about the code.
TO RE-RECORD after an intentional change: re-read the handler, confirm the verdict still holds,
then run `node scripts/check-authz-guards.mjs --print-digest <path>` and paste the new value
with a fresh `checked` date. Re-recording without re-reading is the one thing that makes this
file a lie.
TO REMOVE an entry: give the route a real gate. That is always the better fix.
There are no globs and no wildcards here on purpose — a directory-wide assertion is exactly the
blanket-green failure ADR-970 names. One line per route, one reason per line.

verdicts.public: Anonymous by design. No caller-scoped data crosses the boundary; the response is the same for every visitor, or the write is deliberately identity-free.
verdicts.token-credential: The URL token IS the credential. The handler verifies it (HMAC decode / signed-state) before trusting anything, and the data is scoped to whatever that token resolves to.
verdicts.model-gated: No gate in the route on purpose: the authorization is enforced by the RPC / loader it calls, which self-scopes to the publicly visible set. The route can only narrow, never widen.
verdicts.delegated: The gate lives in the server action or helper this route forwards to, which verifies the caller's token itself. Same posture as `// authz-delegated:` in the lib scan.
verdicts.self-scoped: Acts only on the caller's own session; there is no other principal it could act on.

app/(help)/help/ask/route.ts.reason: Public 'Ask Vera' help endpoint — the help centre itself is public. Reads no caller identity and returns only RAG answers over published help content. Per-IP rate limited (denial-of-wallet, not authz).

app/(main)/e/c/[token]/route.ts.reason: Email click-tracking redirect. decodeSendToken HMAC-authenticates the token and verifyClickUrl binds the exact destination to it, so `u` cannot be swapped even by a holder of a real token. Fail-safe: anything short of all checks redirects to the site root.

app/(main)/e/o/[token]/route.ts.reason: Email open-tracking pixel. decodeSendToken HMAC-authenticates the token before any event is recorded; a forged token records nothing. Always returns the 1x1 GIF so a recipient never sees a broken image.

app/(main)/people/[handle]/vcard/route.t.reason: Public 'Save contact' vCard behind a member's own profile QR. Reads through the admin client but selects only columns the public profile page already shows, and buildVcf emits ONLY the fields the member opted into via `vcard`; 404 when they have not enabled a card.

app/api/check-handle/route.ts.reason: Handle-availability probe for signup (LIVE-031 re-read). Anonymous by design and per-IP rate limited; the whole response is one boolean over the handle_is_available SECURITY DEFINER RPC, which never says WHOSE row holds a taken handle. The auth.getUser() inside `if (excludeUserId)` is not a gate: it only lets a signed-in member re-check their OWN handle without being told it is taken, and every other path answers without it.

app/api/csp-report/route.ts.reason: CSP violation sink. Browsers post reports with no session, so it cannot be authenticated. Stores nothing, never throws, always 204; the handler only logs three truncated fields.

app/api/site-icons/route.ts.reason: Loom icon picker search over the installed @iconify-json packages (ADR-505). No database, no session, no env read; identical response for every visitor. `q` is truncated and `limit` clamped so a crafted request cannot walk the sets twice.

app/api/status/error-budget/route.ts.reason: Read-only error-budget discovery (H0-8, docs/SLOs.md). Pure arithmetic over lib/observability/slos.ts, which is already published in the docs. No DB, no env, no secret, no live measurement.

app/api/status/route.ts.reason: Read-only status index (H0-8). Serves the static SLO contract, VERCEL_GIT_*/VERCEL_ENV build identity, and monitoring.sentry - a boolean derived in lib/observability/sentry.ts, never the DSN (LIVE-053). Its own route.test.ts fails the suite on ANY other process.env read in the file, which is what keeps the no-secret promise true.

app/api/status/slos/route.ts.reason: Read-only SLO discovery (H0-8). Serves the static targets from lib/observability/slos.ts, the same numbers as docs/SLOs.md. No DB, no env, no secret, no live measurement.

app/api/unsubscribe/route.ts.reason: RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe. Mailbox providers POST with no session by spec. The handler forwards to processUnsubscribe / processSpaceUnsubscribe (app/unsubscribe/actions.ts), which verify the signed `t` token themselves; the route never touches the DB.

app/api/vitals/route.ts.reason: Core Web Vitals field sink, anonymous by design: vitals describe the page and device, not a member. Writes through the admin client but never resolves or stores a profile_id (rows land with profile_id NULL and surface NULL), which is what keeps it outside the `analytics` consent scope. Batch cap + normalizer bound each request. Re-read 2026-08-17 after LIVE-036 replaced the inline props literal with vitalProps(v): the change adds `vp`, the viewport BUCKET, which is a property of the page view and not of the person (ADR-922). Nothing about the boundary moved - the handler still takes no session, reads no headers or cookies, and writes profile_id null on every row whatever the payload claims, which app/api/vitals/route.test.ts now asserts with an attacker-shaped payload. The `public` verdict holds.

app/auth/callback/route.ts.reason: Supabase PKCE / magic-link landing (LIVE-031 re-read). The one-time `code` in the URL IS the credential: exchangeCodeForSession verifies it with Supabase and mints the session, and no branch below runs unless that exchange succeeded — a missing or bad code redirects to /sign-in with an error. The auth.getUser() the scan used to detect is three branches down inside a swallowed analytics block, so it never gated anything; the redirect target is separately clamped to a same-origin path. RE-READ 2026-08-18 (LIVE-043): the only change is the FAILURE redirect, which now sends a fixed code (?error=callback) instead of a free-text sentence, plus a comment correction naming app/sign-in/actions.ts as the cookie writer. No gate was added, moved or removed, and the change strictly narrows what a caller can put on the sign-in page. Verdict unchanged.

app/auth/signout/route.ts.reason: Signs out whatever session the request carries and clears the impersonation cookie. There is no other principal it could act on, and it is POST-only so a prefetched GET cannot trigger it.

app/dev/og-root-card/route.tsx.reason: Dev-only generator for the committed root share card (ADR-1002). Renders a pure function of build-time constants (SITE_NAME, SITE_TAGLINE, hero.jpg, logo) — no DB, no session, no caller input. Output is identical bytes on every request.

app/events/[slug]/event.ics/route.ts.reason: Unauthenticated .ics export by design (SEC-9): the link is the share. It cannot leak more than the public event page because a draft / private / circle_only / cancelled event is MASKED in-handler — generic title, no venue, no description, STATUS only.

app/events/calendar.ics/route.ts.reason: Master public calendar feed (EC3, ADR-800). Calendar apps poll with no cookie. public_calendar_feed() takes no arguments and self-gates entirely in-function (published + PUBLIC only, non-cancelled, upcoming, network-visible active spaces), so the route has no way to widen it.

app/events/calendar/[token]/route.ts.reason: Personal subscribable ICS feed (Events B-4). The [token] in the path IS the credential — a member's own secret, rotatable — and the feed contains only events they personally RSVP'd to. Resolved with the admin client exactly like the per-event .ics route.

app/llms-full.txt/route.ts.reason: AIO corpus for answer engines (docs/CONTENT-VOICE §8). Published help articles plus the pricing ladder read from lib/pricing/pricing-grid.ts — the same model /pricing renders. Everything it emits is already on a public page.

app/llms.txt/route.ts.reason: Curated AIO brand summary (ADR-916). Reads through the admin client for live public counts and the operator's pricing config, all of which /pricing and the public pages already show. No caller identity anywhere.

app/podcasts/[spaceSlug]/[showSlug]/rss..reason: Public podcast RSS (Airwaves P3, ADR-608). Apple/Spotify/Overcast poll with no cookie, so it must resolve anonymously. assembleShowFeed IS the visibility floor: it returns null for a missing / draft / private-feed Show, and the route 404s all three identically (no existence leak).

app/q/[slug]/route.ts.reason: Universal QR / dynamic-code resolver (LIVE-031 re-read). The pre-gate admin read is the code row itself, looked up by the PUBLIC slug printed on the poster — service-role only because qr_codes carries no client read policy — and nothing caller-scoped is projected. getMyProfileId() is not the gate; it answers WHO scanned. Every side effect (scan log, joinCircle, checkInEvent, captureQrContact, lead grab) is bound to that session-resolved profile id, never to a client-supplied one, and an anonymous scanner only ever gets cookies plus a redirect.

app/spaces/[slug]/calendar.ics/route.ts.reason: Public per-Space ICS feed (EC1, ADR-800). The handler refuses a private or suspended space BEFORE reading events, then hands the space_id to space_public_calendar_feed, which returns only published, public/unlisted, non-cancelled events.
